findings.actor: UVC와 V4L2 제어 처리 및 공통 파이프라인 핸들러입니다.
findings.timing: 제어 변환과 설정 이후 오류 전파 및 취소까지입니다.
findings.scope: 미실행 조사 계획이며 전체 제어 적용 또는 롤백을 보장하지 않습니다.
findings.reason: 영문은 무시되는 개별 반환값과 취소로 이어지는 설정 오류를 구분하고, error_idx 조사 조건과 적용·롤백에 관한 유보를 보존합니다.
findings.claim_quote: The plan is to distinguish cases where an individual processControl's negative ret is ignored from cases where a negative setControls ret passes through UVC and leads to cancelRequest, and to record the conversion ret, the number of configured controls, and the setControls ret. The plan first separates the return of 0 for an empty control list from validation failures before the ioctl, and examines that call's error_idx only if the actual control ioctl was executed. Even when control processing precedes this, the application or rollback of all request controls is not assumed.

findings.condition: UVC 제출 경로에서 cache get에 성공하고 QBUF가 음수를 반환하는 경우이며, cache 부재는 별도 경우입니다.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice, UVC 및 공통 파이프라인 핸들러; 기록은 시험 계획입니다.
findings.timing: QBUF 실패 후 scope_exit와 반환 전파를 확인하고 요청별 통지를 기록합니다.
findings.scope: 선택된 실패 분기와 completeRequest의 제출 순서 반환 계약; 실제 시험 결과는 아닙니다.
findings.reason: 해당 실패 분기는 guard를 해제하기 전에 반환하며 UVC와 공통 제출 경로가 음수 반환과 취소를 처리합니다. 버퍼 완료와 요청 완료의 구분 및 Fatal 사례의 한정도 근거와 부합합니다.
findings.claim_quote: cache get 성공 뒤 VIDIOC_QBUF에 음수를 주입하는 시험에서는 확보 index, ioctl ret, 이번 scope_exit의 put 횟수와 해당 항목의 free 상태, 이번 버퍼의 신규 queuedBuffers_ 등록 부재를 기록합니다. 원래 음수 ret의 전달과 공통 취소를 대조하고, 버퍼 완료가 요청을 자동 완료하지 않으며 요청은 명시적으로 완료되고 제출 순서대로 반환되는 조건에 맞춰 요청별 알림 횟수를 기록합니다. cache_ 자체 부재의 Fatal은 정상 음수 반환이나 cancelRequest 도달을 보장하지 않는 별도 경우로 다룹니다.

findings.condition: UVC submission reaches QBUF after a successful cache get and QBUF returns a negative value; absent cache is a separate case.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice, UVC and the common pipeline handler; recording is planned.
findings.timing: After QBUF failure, check scope exit and return propagation, then record request notifications.
findings.scope: The selected failure path and the submission-order return contract; no executed test is asserted.
findings.reason: The guard runs on the failure return, and the UVC and common submission paths propagate the error and cancel the request. The translation preserves the completion distinction and Fatal qualification.
findings.claim_quote: In a test that injects a negative result into VIDIOC_QBUF after a successful cache get, the plan is to record the acquired index, ioctl ret, the number of put calls by this scope_exit and the free state of the corresponding entry, and the absence of a new queuedBuffers_ registration for this buffer. The plan is to check propagation of the original negative ret and common cancellation, and record the notification count for each request in accordance with the conditions that buffer completion does not automatically complete the request, requests are completed explicitly, and they are returned in submission order. A Fatal caused by the absence of cache_ itself is treated as a separate case that does not guarantee a normal negative return or reaching cancelRequest.

findings.condition: DQBUF ioctl 오류 또는 성공적으로 반환된 예상 밖 인덱스를 각각 주입하는 경우입니다.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice의 dequeueBuffer와 bufferAvailable; 기록은 조사 계획입니다.
findings.timing: 해당 dequeue 호출과 그에 따른 단일 알림 분기를 관찰합니다.
findings.scope: 한 번의 bufferReady 미발행에 한정하며 이후 장치 동작을 보장하지 않습니다.
findings.reason: 두 오류 분기는 nullptr을 반환하고 bufferAvailable은 이 경우 signal을 발행하지 않습니다. 제안된 관찰은 영구 정지나 취소를 실행 결과로 단정하지 않습니다.
findings.claim_quote: ioctl 오류와 예상 밖 인덱스를 각각 주입하면 해당 dequeueBuffer 호출은 nullptr을 반환하고 bufferAvailable은 bufferReady를 내지 않는 분기를 관찰하며, 각 시점의 ret, index, queuedBuffers_, 요청 pending 및 큐 선두 status를 기록 항목으로 제안합니다. 이 한 번의 알림 부재를 영구 정지, 자동 취소 또는 하드웨어 롤백의 보장으로 확대하지 않습니다.

findings.condition: An ioctl error and a successfully returned unexpected DQBUF index are injected separately.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice dequeueBuffer and bufferAvailable; recording is proposed.
findings.timing: The observation concerns the corresponding dequeue call and notification branch.
findings.scope: A single absence of bufferReady, with no guarantee about subsequent device behavior.
findings.reason: Both branches return nullptr and bufferAvailable emits no bufferReady for that invocation. The translation does not assert permanent stop, cancellation, rollback, or an executed test.
findings.claim_quote: The proposed observation is to inject an ioctl error and an unexpected index separately and observe the branch where the corresponding dequeueBuffer call returns nullptr and bufferAvailable does not emit bufferReady. The proposed items to record at each point are ret, index, queuedBuffers_, the request's pending state, and the status of the request at the front of the queue. This single absence of a notification is not treated as a guarantee of a permanent stop, automatic cancellation, or hardware rollback.

findings.condition: 유효하게 dequeue된 버퍼에 오류 플래그가 있고 해당 UVC 완료 경로가 실행되며 다른 취소 원인이 없는 경우입니다.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice와 UVC가 완료를 처리하고 버퍼 호출자는 수명을 보장할 책임이 있습니다.
findings.timing: 버퍼 완료 호출 뒤 요청 완료 호출; 애플리케이션 반환은 제출 순서를 따릅니다.
findings.scope: 정상 dequeue 경로의 소스 계약과 미실행 관찰 계획이며 정지 중 버퍼 취소와 구별됩니다.
findings.reason: FrameError는 FrameCancelled와 다르고 UVC는 버퍼 다음에 요청을 완료합니다. 한 번의 pending 제거와 콜백까지의 유효성은 각각 완료 규칙과 호출자 의무이며 실제 관찰 결과가 아닙니다.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: 유효하게 dequeue된 버퍼의 V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR와 FrameError를 기록하고, UVC가 해당 상태를 유지한 채 completeBuffer 다음에 completeRequest를 호출하는 경로를 확인합니다. pending에서 버퍼가 한 번 제거되는 횟수와 요청의 제출·완료 통지 순서, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되는 수명을 기록하며, 다른 취소 원인이 없을 때 가능한 RequestComplete를 FrameError와 별도로 기록합니다.

findings.condition: A validly dequeued buffer has the error flag, the specified UVC completion path runs, and no other cause cancels the request.
findings.actor: V4L2VideoDevice and UVC process completion; the buffer caller is responsible for its lifetime.
findings.timing: Buffer completion is called before request completion; application returns follow submission order.
findings.scope: The normal dequeue source path and an unexecuted observation plan, distinct from cancellation during stop.
findings.reason: FrameError does not itself mark the request cancelled, and UVC calls buffer completion before request completion. One pending removal is a completion rule and buffer validity through the callback is a caller obligation, not an observed result.

findings.claim_quote: The plan is to record V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR and FrameError for a validly dequeued buffer and check the path where UVC calls completeBuffer followed by completeRequest while retaining that status. The plan also records the count of buffer removals from pending, which should occur once, the order of request submission and completion notifications, and the period for which the buffer remains valid through the request completion callback. Any possible RequestComplete when there is no other cause of cancellation is recorded separately from FrameError.

findings.condition: 정상 정지와 STREAMOFF·releaseBuffers 실패를 구분하며, 후속 DQBUF 검사는 cache reset과 잔존 notifier·큐가 겹치는 경우를 대상으로 합니다.
findings.actor: 공통 PipelineHandler, UVC stopDevice 및 조사자
findings.timing: 대기 큐 분리 후 장치 정지와 대기 요청 취소를 추적하고, 실패 뒤 후속 dequeue를 확인합니다.
findings.scope: 요청·버퍼 완료와 큐 상태에 관한 미실행 조사 계획입니다.
findings.reason: 소스는 분리된 요청의 순번 등록과 제출 순서 반환을 뒷받침하며, UVC 실패 경로와 알려진 인덱스의 cache 접근을 별도로 조사할 근거를 제공합니다. 안전한 처리가 이미 관찰됐다는 주장은 아닙니다. 실패 사례의 반환값은 각 호출을 구분해야 하며 Camera::stop의 정상 경로가 장치 오류를 전달한다는 뜻은 아닙니다.
findings.claim_quote: 정상 정지에서는 waitingRequests_ 분리 후 장치 요청의 취소 완료, 분리된 요청의 순번 등록과 제출 순서에 따른 반환을 추적하고, 요청별·버퍼별 완료 횟수와 queuedRequests_·waitingRequests_의 잔존 및 정지 중 재투입을 기록합니다. STREAMOFF 실패와 releaseBuffers 실패를 별도 사례로 두고 각각의 ret, state_, cache_, queuedBuffers_, queuedRequests_, ASSERT 도달 및 정지 중 재투입을 기록하며, 실패 시 0 반환이나 모든 버퍼 반환을 기대하지 않고, STREAMOFF 실패 후 cache_ reset과 잔존 notifier·큐가 겹치면 알려진 인덱스의 후속 DQBUF에서 cache_->put 접근이 안전하게 처리되는지 확인합니다.

findings.condition: Normal stop is distinguished from STREAMOFF and releaseBuffers failures; the later DQBUF check is conditional on a reset cache and remaining notifier and queue.
findings.actor: The common pipeline handler, UVC stopDevice, and investigator
findings.timing: The plan tracks device stop and detached-request cancellation after the waiting queue is detached, then examines any subsequent dequeue.
findings.scope: An unexecuted investigation of request and buffer completions and queue state.
findings.reason: The translation preserves the conditional plan. The sources support sequence assignment and submission-order return, and identify the failure path to investigate without establishing a safe runtime outcome. Return values must be attributed to the individual calls; the normal Camera::stop return does not propagate device errors.
findings.claim_quote: For a normal stop, the plan is to track the completion of device request cancellation after waitingRequests_ is detached, the assignment of sequence numbers to the detached requests, and their return in submission order, and to record completion counts per request and per buffer, whether queuedRequests_ and waitingRequests_ remain, and whether requests are requeued during the stop. STREAMOFF failure and releaseBuffers failure are treated as separate cases; for each, the plan is to record ret, state_, cache_, queuedBuffers_, queuedRequests_, whether ASSERT is reached, and whether requests are requeued during the stop. The plan does not expect a return value of 0 or the return of all buffers on failure, and checks whether access to cache_->put is handled safely on a subsequent DQBUF for a known index if a cache_ reset after STREAMOFF failure coincides with a remaining notifier and queue.

findings.condition: 허용된 재진입과 별도 허용 문서가 필요한 콜백 중첩을 구분하고, 실행 중 접근 검사를 통과한 stop 경로를 확인합니다.
findings.actor: doQueueRequests, Signal 발신자, 요청 소유자 및 각 수신자
findings.timing: Blocking 호출의 반환과 지연 수신자 각각의 마지막 사용을 분리하며 삭제·재사용 전에 수명을 조정합니다.
findings.scope: 스레드·수명에 관한 검증 계획이며 실제 실행이나 모든 수신자의 종료 보장이 아닙니다.
findings.reason: 재귀를 고려한 pop 순서와 일반적인 콜백 중첩 제한은 서로 다른 조건입니다. Blocking 반환은 별도 Queued 수신자의 마지막 사용을 증명하지 않으며, 발신자의 유효성 의무와 소유자의 조정 여부를 조사하는 계획도 이에 부합합니다.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

/**
 * \fn Signal::connect

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: For permitted doQueueRequests reentry, the pop and submission order and the number of submissions per request are recorded to check for duplicate submissions; nested entry into the same function from a callback is not performed without separate documentation permitting it. The current and receiver threads for Direct and delayed Queued reception, cookie, sequence, callback entry and return, events before and after stop, and object lifetimes are recorded. The investigation separately checks whether the execution reached the normal path in which Camera::stop, having passed the access check while running, calls PipelineHandler::stop with ConnectionTypeBlocking, and distinguishes the Blocking return from each separate Queued receiver's last use and termination. It verifies that the Signal sender keeps pointers and references valid and that the request owner synchronizes every delayed receiver's last use through completion and release coordination before deletion or reuse; a request completion signal or the return of one handler is not treated as the end of use by all delayed receivers.

findings.claim_quote: The public virtual CPU probe was run three times. In each run, four requests were reported as RequestComplete, four as RequestCancelled, and there were 24 callbacks. There were 72 callbacks in total. In the public Virtual2 virtual probe on Ubuntu WSL2, Auto and Queued callbacks ran on the receiving object's main thread, while Direct callbacks ran on a different thread. Markers near callback entry and return for requests cancelled during stop were observed after stop-return for Auto and Queued, and between stop-enter and stop-return for Direct. The stop-enter and stop-return markers are application markers before and after the camera->stop() call, not exact instruction boundaries inside the function.

findings.condition: 준비 대기가 정지 취소로 중단되지 않은 경로와 별도의 정지 취소 경로를 구분합니다.
findings.actor: Request::Private의 준비, 타임아웃 및 취소 경로와 공통 PipelineHandler::stop.
findings.timing: 펜스가 없을 때 즉시, 마지막 펜스 처리 후 또는 타임아웃 취소 후 prepared를 발행합니다.
findings.scope: 소스의 준비 및 정지 취소 경로에 관한 설명입니다.
findings.reason: 준비 완료와 타임아웃 경로는 준비 구현에 부합하고, 정지의 별도 cancel 경로는 notifier와 타이머를 정리하면서 자체적으로 prepared를 발행하지 않습니다. 관련 문서와 번역도 이 경로 구분에 충돌하지 않습니다.
findings.claim_quote: Request::Private::prepare의 정상 경로는 정지 취소로 준비 대기가 중단되지 않은 경우입니다. 대기할 펜스가 없으면 즉시 prepared 신호를 발행하고, 대기 중인 마지막 펜스가 신호되면 prepared 신호를 발행합니다. 타이머가 설정되어 만료되면 요청을 취소한 뒤 prepared 신호를 발행합니다. 별도의 정지 취소는 타이머와 notifier를 정리하며, 그 취소 경로 자체는 prepared 신호를 발행하지 않습니다.

findings.claim_quote: The normal path for Request::Private::prepare is when waiting for preparation is not interrupted by cancellation during stop. If there are no fences to wait for, the prepared signal is emitted immediately; when the last fence being waited on is signaled, the prepared signal is emitted. If a timer is set and expires, the request is canceled and then the prepared signal is emitted. Separate cancellation during stop cleans up the timer and notifier, and that cancellation path itself does not emit the prepared signal.

findings.condition: 큐 크기가 한도와 같거나 선두 요청이 미준비인 경우와 이미 취소된 요청을 처리하는 경우.

findings.reason: 두 break 조건과 후위 증가, 취소된 요청의 completeRequest 호출 및 반환이 소스와 일치합니다. 관련 문서와 영문 번역도 같은 객체와 순서를 설명합니다.
findings.claim_quote: doQueueRequests에서 queuedRequests_의 크기가 maxQueuedRequestsDevice_와 같으면 break로 반복을 중단합니다. doQueueRequests에서 waitingRequests_ 선두 요청의 prepared_가 false이면 break를 실행하여 while 반복을 중단합니다. doQueueRequest는 요청을 queuedRequests_에 추가한 뒤 sequence_에 requestSequence_의 증가 전 값을 대입하고 requestSequence_를 증가시킵니다. doQueueRequest에서 이미 취소된 요청을 뜻하는 cancelled_ 조건이 참이면 completeRequest(request)를 호출하고 doQueueRequest에서 반환합니다.

findings.claim_quote: In doQueueRequests, if the size of queuedRequests_ equals maxQueuedRequestsDevice_, the loop is terminated with break. In doQueueRequests, if prepared_ of the request at the front of waitingRequests_ is false, break is executed to terminate the while loop. After adding the request to queuedRequests_, doQueueRequest assigns the pre-increment value of requestSequence_ to sequence_ and increments requestSequence_. In doQueueRequest, if the cancelled_ condition, which indicates that the request has already been cancelled, is true, doQueueRequest calls completeRequest(request) and returns from doQueueRequest.

In doQueueRequest, if ret, the return value of queueRequestDevice, is nonzero, doQueueRequest calls cancelRequest(request). The pipeline handler implementing queueRequestDevice must program the device so that the request's parameters are applied to the frames captured in the buffers provided in the request.

findings.actor: The pipeline handler calls the completion functions; Request::Private performs internal cancellation and status transition.

sources.source_quote:
\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

/**
 * \brief Signal request completion

findings.claim_quote: completeBuffer와 completeRequest는 모두 CameraManager 스레드에서 호출해야 합니다. cancelRequest는 내부 취소를 먼저 수행한 뒤 completeRequest를 호출합니다. 내부 취소는 각 대기 버퍼를 취소하고 해당 버퍼의 bufferCompleted를 발생시킨 다음, cancelled_를 true로 설정하고 대기 버퍼 목록을 비웁니다. 이후 completeRequest에서 호출하는 Request::Private::complete()는 cancelled_에 따라 요청 상태에 RequestCancelled를 대입합니다.

\brief Complete a buffer for a request
 * \param[in] request The request the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The buffer that has completed
 *
 * This function shall be called by pipeline handlers to signal completion of
 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
 *
 * \context This function shall be called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return True if all buffers contained in the request have completed, false
 * otherwise
 */
bool PipelineHandler::completeBuffer(Request *request, FrameBuffer *buffer)
{
	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	camera->bufferCompleted.emit(request, buffer);
	return request->_d()->completeBuffer(buffer);
}

\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequest()
 * \brief Queue a request
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the pipeline handler for
 * processing. The request is first added to the internal list of waiting
 * requests which have to be prepared to make sure they are ready for being
 * queued to the pipeline handler.
 *
 * The queue of waiting requests is iterated and up to \a
 * maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ prepared requests are passed to the pipeline handler
 * in the same order they have been queued by calling this function.
 *
 * If a Request fails during the preparation phase or if the pipeline handler
 * fails in queuing the request to the hardware the request is cancelled.
 *
 * Keeping track of queued requests ensures automatic completion of all requests
 * when the pipeline handler is stopped with stop(). Request completion shall be
 * signalled by the pipeline handler using the completeRequest() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::queueRequest(Request *request)
{
	LIBCAMERA_TRACEPOINT(request_queue, request);

	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	Camera::Private *data = camera->_d();
	data->waitingRequests_.push(request);

	request->_d()->prepare(300ms);
}

findings.claim_quote: Camera::queueRequest는 patchControlList로 요청의 AeEnable을 전처리한 뒤 ConnectionTypeQueued를 사용해 PipelineHandler::queueRequest에 요청을 전달합니다. 카메라 상태는 함수가 끝날 때까지 바뀔 수 있으며, PipelineHandler::queueRequest가 이 상태 변경을 처리하므로 이 부분에는 잠금이 필요하지 않습니다. CameraManager 스레드에서 호출되는 PipelineHandler::queueRequest는 요청을 waitingRequests_에 넣은 뒤 prepare(300ms)를 시작합니다. 소스 주석에 따르면 준비 단계에서 요청이 실패하면 해당 요청을 취소합니다.

findings.claim_quote: Camera::queueRequest preprocesses the request's AeEnable using patchControlList and then passes the request to PipelineHandler::queueRequest using ConnectionTypeQueued. The camera state may change until the function ends, and no locking is needed for this part because PipelineHandler::queueRequest handles the state change. Called from the CameraManager thread, PipelineHandler::queueRequest puts the request in waitingRequests_ and then starts prepare(300ms). According to the source comment, if a request fails during preparation, that request is cancelled.
