/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

 * The frame has been captured with success and contains valid data. All fields

 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameError
 * The frame data is partly or fully corrupted, missing or otherwise invalid.
 * This can for instance indicate a hardware transmission error, or invalid data
 * produced by the sensor during its startup phase. The sequence and timestamp
 * fields of the FrameMetadata structure is valid, all the other fields may be
 * invalid.
 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameCancelled
 * Capture stopped before the frame completed. The frame data is not valid. All
 * fields of the FrameMetadata structure but the status field are invalid.
 * \var FrameMetadata::FrameStartup
 * The frame has been successfully captured. However, the IPA is in a
 * cold-start or reset phase and will result in image quality parameters
 * producing unusable images. Applications are recommended to not consume these
 * frames. All other fields of the FrameMetadata structure are valid.

scenario-queue_request/dispatch/prepare.text:
\fn PipelineHandler::queueRequest()
 * \brief Queue a request
 * \param[in] request The request to queue
 *
 * This function queues a capture request to the pipeline handler for
 * processing. The request is first added to the internal list of waiting
 * requests which have to be prepared to make sure they are ready for being
 * queued to the pipeline handler.
 *
 * The queue of waiting requests is iterated and up to \a
 * maxQueuedRequestsDevice_ prepared requests are passed to the pipeline handler
 * in the same order they have been queued by calling this function.
 *
 * If a Request fails during the preparation phase or if the pipeline handler
 * fails in queuing the request to the hardware the request is cancelled.
 *
 * Keeping track of queued requests ensures automatic completion of all requests
 * when the pipeline handler is stopped with stop(). Request completion shall be
 * signalled by the pipeline handler using the completeRequest() function.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 */
void PipelineHandler::queueRequest(Request *request)
{
	LIBCAMERA_TRACEPOINT(request_queue, request);

	Camera *camera = request->_d()->camera();
	Camera::Private *data = camera->_d();
	data->waitingRequests_.push(request);

	request->_d()->prepare(300ms);
}

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *

 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a

 * be left unmodified.

 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence

 */

findings.claim_quote: `Camera::Private::disconnect()`는 현재 상태가 `CameraRunning`일 때만 `CameraConfigured`를 저장하며, 다른 상태에서는 이 저장을 생략합니다. 이후 상태와 관계없이 `disconnected_`를 `true`로 설정합니다. 주석에 따르면 상태 변경의 목적은 하드웨어가 제거될 때 카메라가 실행 중이었다면 애플리케이션이 카메라를 삭제하기 전에 자원을 해제하고 `release()`를 호출할 수 있도록 하는 것입니다.

\class CameraManager
 * \brief Provide access and manage all cameras in the system
 *
 * The camera manager is the entry point to libcamera. It enumerates devices,
 * associates them with pipeline managers, and provides access to the cameras
 * in the system to applications. The manager owns all Camera objects and
 * handles hot-plugging and hot-unplugging to manage the lifetime of cameras.
 *
 * To interact with libcamera, an application starts by creating a camera
 * manager instance. Only a single instance of the camera manager may exist at
 * a time. Attempting to create a second instance without first deleting the
 * existing instance results in undefined behaviour.
 *
 * The manager is initially stopped, and shall be started with start(). This
 * will enumerate all the cameras present in the system, which can then be
 * listed with list() and retrieved with get().
 *
 * Cameras are shared through std::shared_ptr<>, ensuring that a camera will
 * stay valid until the last reference is released without requiring any special
 * action from the application. Once the application has released all the
 * references it held to cameras, the camera manager can be stopped with
 * stop().
 */

CameraManager *CameraManager::self_

 * lifetime of camera instances with std::shared_ptr<>. Instances shall be
 * created with the create() function which returns a shared pointer. The
 * Camera constructors and destructor are private, to prevent instances from
 * being constructed and destroyed manually.
 *
 * \section camera_operation

findings.claim_quote: `CameraManager`는 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며, 애플리케이션에 카메라 접근을 제공하고 카메라 객체를 소유하면서 핫플러그와 핫언플러그에 따른 수명을 관리하는 libcamera의 진입점입니다. `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 한 번에 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 추가 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *

 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence

 */

findings.claim_quote: `PipelineHandler::completeBuffer`는 `bufferCompleted.emit` 뒤에 `Request::Private::completeBuffer`를 호출해 `pending_`에서 버퍼를 제거하고 버퍼의 요청 연결을 해제하며, `ConnectionTypeDirect` 콜백은 송신자 스레드에서 즉시 동기 실행되므로 내부 갱신 전에 실행될 수 있습니다. 호출자는 `bufferCompleted` 신호만으로 요청 완료나 삭제·재사용 시점을 판단해서는 안 되며, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼를 유효하게 유지해야 합니다.

findings.condition: A의 직접 버퍼 완료 수신자에서 B의 addBuffer가 같은 버퍼의 연결을 실제로 변경한 경우입니다.
findings.actor: B의 Request::addBuffer와 A의 내부 completeBuffer입니다.
findings.timing: A의 신호 발행 중 B 연결이 설정된 뒤, A의 내부 갱신이 실행될 때입니다.
findings.scope: 동일 버퍼의 요청 연결과 지연 수신자 수명에 관한 별도 확인입니다.
findings.reason: 성공한 addBuffer는 버퍼의 요청 연결을 B로 설정하고, 뒤따르는 A의 내부 completeBuffer는 같은 버퍼의 연결을 지웁니다. 조건부 가능성은 비교 주장 및 두 언어판과 일치하며 일괄 취소 경로를 일반화하지 않습니다.

findings.claim_quote: `Request::Private::completeBuffer()`는 `pending_`에서 버퍼를 지운 뒤 `setRequest(nullptr)`을 호출하지만, `doCancelRequest()`는 대기 중인 각 버퍼를 취소하고 완료 신호를 보낸 뒤 `pending_.clear()`를 호출하며 같은 연결 해제는 호출하지 않습니다. `FrameBuffer::request()`가 반환하는 포인터는 `Request::addBuffer()`로 연결된 때부터 버퍼가 완료될 때까지만 유효하므로, 취소 뒤 저장된 값이 비널이어도 유효한 `Request` 포인터나 소유권 또는 수명 연장으로 해석해서는 안 됩니다.

findings.condition: 버퍼와 포인터 인수의 유효성을 유지하며, 신호되지 않은 펜스로 타임아웃된 버퍼를 다른 요청에 재사용하는 경우입니다.
findings.actor: addBuffer와 invokeMethod의 호출자 및 애플리케이션입니다.
findings.timing: 각각 요청 완료 콜백, 메서드 호출 및 다른 요청에서의 재사용 전까지입니다.
findings.scope: 호출자의 의무와 별도의 실행 관찰 계획입니다.
findings.reason: 유효성 및 펜스 회수 의무가 소스와 일치합니다. 관찰 항목은 실행 결과를 주장하지 않으며 한영 문장도 일치합니다.

 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event

 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference

findings.claim_quote: 마지막 버퍼 알림은 관찰했지만 요청 완료 콜백은 아직 관찰하지 못한 경우, 그 관측만으로 내부 추적 갱신이나 `completeRequest` 호출이 아직 남았다고 단정할 수 없습니다. 이 알림은 버퍼 유효성 유지 기한이 끝났다는 근거가 아니므로, 버퍼 유효성을 깨뜨리는 해제나 다른 요청에 연결하는 작업의 안전성을 알림만으로 판정할 수 없습니다. 모든 재사용이 일괄적으로 금지되는 것은 아니며, 다른 요청에 연결할 수 있는지는 적용되는 API와 동기화 계약 및 버퍼 유효성 유지를 별도로 대조해야 합니다.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: 앞의 정상 완료 예와 별도로, 제출 큐의 선두 요청 A와 요청 B가 모두 `RequestPending`인 시점에 파이프라인 핸들러가 `completeRequest(B)` 대신 `cancelRequest(B)`를 호출하는 경우입니다. `Request::Private::doCancelRequest`는 B의 `pending_` 버퍼를 각각 취소하고 `bufferCompleted`를 발생시킨 뒤 `cancelled_`를 `true`로 설정하고 `pending_`를 비웁니다. `cancelRequest`는 `cancel` 다음에 `completeRequest`를 호출하며, `Request::Private::complete`는 B의 상태로 `RequestCancelled`를 선택합니다. 선두 A가 여전히 `RequestPending`이면 B의 애플리케이션 반환은 지연되며, 버퍼 수명과 핸들러의 요청 접근에는 앞에서 설명한 공통 규칙이 적용됩니다.

findings.condition: 유효한 Fence를 addBuffer에 전달한 경우입니다.
findings.actor: addBuffer 호출자와 대상 버퍼입니다.
findings.timing: 호출 성공 시 소유권이 이동하고 실패 시 전달된 펜스는 유지됩니다.
findings.scope: addBuffer 호출의 성공·실패에 따른 펜스 소유권입니다.
findings.reason: 성공과 실패의 소유권 및 변경 여부가 API 계약과 일치하며 한영 문장도 일치합니다.

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.

 * associates them with pipeline managers, and provides access to the cameras
 * in the system to applications. The manager owns all Camera objects and
 * handles hot-plugging and hot-unplugging to manage the lifetime of cameras.
 *
 * To interact with libcamera, an application starts by creating a camera
 * manager instance. Only a single instance of the camera manager may exist at
 * a time. Attempting to create a second instance without first deleting the
 * existing instance results in undefined behaviour.
 *
 * The manager is initially stopped,

\brief Start the camera manager
 *
 * Start the camera manager and enumerate all devices in the system. Once
 * the start has been confirmed the user is free to list and otherwise
 * interact with cameras in the system until either the camera manager
 * is stopped or the camera is unplugged from the system.
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 */
int CameraManager::start()

 * \return List of all available cameras
 */
std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Camera>> CameraManager::cameras() const

}

 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request

 *

 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: If the last buffer notification has been observed but the request completion callback has not yet been observed, that observation alone does not establish that the internal tracking update or the completeRequest call is still pending. This notification is not evidence that the period for which the buffer must remain valid has ended, so the notification alone cannot establish whether releasing it in a way that invalidates the buffer or attaching it to another request is safe. Reuse is not categorically prohibited; whether it can be attached to another request must be checked separately against the applicable API and synchronization contracts and the requirement to maintain buffer validity.

Request::Private::doCancelRequest는 B의 pending_ 버퍼를 각각 취소하고 bufferCompleted를 발생시킨 뒤 cancelled_를 true로 설정하고 pending_를 비웁니다. cancelRequest는 cancel 다음에 completeRequest를 호출하며, Request::Private::complete는 B의 상태로 RequestCancelled를 선택합니다. 선두 A가 여전히 RequestPending이면 B의 애플리케이션 반환은 지연되며, 버퍼 수명과 핸들러의 요청 접근에는 앞에서 설명한 공통 규칙이 적용됩니다.

findings.condition: Both A at the submission queue head and B are pending when the handler cancels B; A remains pending when return is considered.
findings.actor: The pipeline handler and B's internal request handling code.
findings.timing: B's pending buffers are cancelled and signalled before its cancelled status is selected; B's return is delayed while A remains pending at the head.
findings.scope: The specified cancellation case, submission-ordered return, buffer lifetime and handler access.
findings.reason: The cancellation path processes pending buffers, sets cancellation state and invokes completion. The completion loop stops at a pending head, and the common lifetime and access rules apply. The Korean claim and relevant peers agree on these conditions and effects.

findings.claim_quote: Separate from the preceding normal completion example, this is a case where the pipeline handler calls cancelRequest(B) instead of completeRequest(B) when both request A at the front of the submission queue and request B are RequestPending. Request::Private::doCancelRequest cancels each of B's pending_ buffers and emits bufferCompleted, then sets cancelled_ to true and clears pending_. cancelRequest calls completeRequest after cancel, and Request::Private::complete selects RequestCancelled as B's status. findings.claim_quote: Request::Private::completeBuffer() removes the buffer from pending_ and then calls setRequest(nullptr), whereas doCancelRequest() cancels each pending buffer, emits a completion signal, and then calls pending_.clear() without making the same disconnection. The pointer returned by FrameBuffer::request() is valid only from the time the buffer is associated through Request::addBuffer() until the buffer completes, so even if the stored value is non-null after cancellation, it must not be interpreted as a valid Request pointer, ownership, or an extension of lifetime.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: The caller must ensure that the buffer passed to Request::addBuffer() remains valid until the request completion callback, and, when passing a pointer argument to Object::invokeMethod(), must ensure that the pointer remains valid until the invoked method executes. If a request times out because a valid fence is not signalled, the application must retrieve the fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request. \class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

 * An application needs to perform a sequence of operations on a camera before
 * it is ready to process requests. The camera needs to be acquired and

 * process requests until it is stopped. When an application is done with a
 * camera, the camera needs to be released.

 * for ensuring their synchronization if necessary.

 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.

findings.claim_quote: In the change verification plan, the sender and request owner coordinate completion and release timing and track and synchronize the last use by each separate ConnectionTypeQueued receiver. They do not end the lifetime of the object passed by deleting or reusing it before confirming the last use by every delayed receiver. The source-based investigation plan is to record, at Signal::emit(), whether the receiver has an Object, the connection type, the current and receiver threads, the event loop, and the states of the request and buffer, and to distinguish callback entry and return and the periods before and after camera stop with application markers. While investigating ConnectionTypeDirect reentrancy and ConnectionTypeQueued delays, the plan is to check the validity of passed pointers and references, the return value of pending_.erase(buffer) in Request::Private::completeBuffer() and the subsequent branch, and whether duplicate completion or request submission after stop occurs.

\brief Add a FrameBuffer with its associated Stream to the Request
 * \param[in] stream The stream the buffer belongs to
 * \param[in] buffer The FrameBuffer to add to the request
 * \param[in] fence The optional fence
 *
 * A reference to the buffer is stored in the request. The caller is responsible
 * for ensuring that the buffer will remain valid until the request complete
 * callback is called.
 *
 * A request can only contain one buffer per stream. If a buffer has already
 * been added to the request for the same stream, this function returns -EEXIST.
 *
 * A Fence can be optionally associated with the \a buffer.
 *
 * When a valid Fence is provided to this function, \a fence is moved to \a
 * buffer and this Request will only be queued to the device once the
 * fences of all its buffers have been correctly signalled. Ownership of the
 * fence will only be taken in case of success, otherwise the fence will
 * be left unmodified.
 *
 * If the \a fence associated with \a buffer isn't signalled, the request will
 * fail after a timeout. The buffer will still contain the fence, which
 * applications must retrieve with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before the buffer
 * can be reused in another request. Attempting to add a buffer that still
 * contains a fence to a request will result in this function returning -EEXIST.
 *
 * \sa FrameBuffer::releaseFence()
 *
 * \return 0 on success or a negative error code otherwise
 * \retval -EEXIST The request already contains a buffer for the stream
 *  or the buffer still references a fence
 * \retval -EINVAL The buffer does not reference a valid Stream
 */
int Request::addBuffer(const Stream *stream, FrameBuffer *buffer,

findings.claim_quote: The plan is to record V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR and FrameError for a validly dequeued buffer and check the path where UVC calls completeBuffer followed by completeRequest while retaining that status. The plan also records the count of buffer removals from pending, which should occur once, the order of request submission and completion notifications, and the period for which the buffer remains valid through the request completion callback. Any possible RequestComplete when there is no other cause of cancellation is recorded separately from FrameError.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

\brief Create a request object for the camera
 * \param[in] cookie Opaque cookie for application use
 *
 * This function creates an empty request for the application to fill with
 * buffers and parameters, and queue for capture.
 *
 * The \a cookie is stored in the request and is accessible through the
 * Request::cookie() function at any time. It is typically used by applications
 * to map the request to an external resource in the request completion
 * handler, and is completely opaque to libcamera.
 *
 * The ownership of the returned request is passed to the caller, which is
 * responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion
 * handler, or reused after resetting its state with Request::reuse().
 *
 * \context This function is \threadsafe. It may only be called when the camera
 * is in the Configured or Running state as defined in \ref camera_operation.
 *
 * \return A pointer to the newly created request, or nullptr on error
 */
std::unique_ptr<Request> Camera::createRequest(uint64_t cookie)

findings.reason: 한국어 원문과 같은 가능성 및 호출자의 의무를 표현하며 소스의 Adjusted 계약에 부합합니다.

sources.source_quote:
\fn CameraConfiguration::validate()
 * \brief Validate and possibly adjust the camera configuration
 *
 * This function adjusts the camera configuration to the closest valid
 * configuration and returns the validation status.
 *
 * \todo Define exactly when to return each status code. Should stream
 * parameters set to 0 by the caller be adjusted without returning Adjusted ?
 * This would potentially be useful for applications but would get in the way
 * in Camera::configure(). Do we need an extra status code to signal this ?
 *
 * \todo Handle validation of buffers count when refactoring the buffers API.
 *
 * \return A CameraConfiguration::Status value that describes the validation
 * status.
 * \retval CameraConfiguration::Invalid The configuration is invalid and can't
 * be adjusted. This may only occur in extreme cases such as when the
 * configuration is empty.
 * \retval CameraConfiguration::Adjusted The configuration has been adjusted
 * and is now valid. Parameters may have changed for any stream, and stream
 * configurations may have been removed. The caller shall check the
 * configuration carefully.
 * \retval CameraConfiguration::Valid The configuration was already valid and
 * hasn't been adjusted.
 */

/**
 * \brief Retrieve a reference to a stream configuration

\retval CameraConfiguration::Adjusted The configuration has been adjusted
 * and is now valid. Parameters may have changed for any stream, and stream
 * configurations may have been removed. The caller shall check the
 * configuration carefully.

findings.claim_quote: Adjusted from CameraConfiguration::validate() means the configuration has been adjusted so that it is valid; parameters may have changed for any stream, or stream configurations may have been removed. A caller that receives Adjusted must check the configuration carefully.

overview.md/creation/2.text: `Camera::createRequest()`가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 전달되며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다.

overview.md/creation/3.text: 호출자는 새 요청을 만드는 대신 같은 요청을 다시 큐에 넣으려면 큐에 넣기 전에 `Request::reuse()`를 호출하여 요청 상태와 연결된 컨트롤을 초기화해야 합니다.

overview.md/creation/4.text: `Request::reuse(ReuseFlag)`는 `ReuseBuffers`를 지정하면 `addBuffer()`로 추가한 기존 버퍼를 유지해 재사용하고, 지정하지 않으면 `bufferMap_`을 비웁니다.

overview.md/discovery/1.text: `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 동시에 하나만 존재해야 합니다. 기존 인스턴스를 먼저 삭제하지 않고 두 번째 인스턴스를 생성하면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

overview.md/responsibility/0.text: `Camera`는 하나의 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 모델링합니다. 장치 구성과 제어, 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주 인터페이스이며, libcamera가 공개하는 중심 객체입니다. libcamera는 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 `std::shared_ptr<>`로 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 `create()`로 생성해야 합니다. `Camera`의 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 수동으로 생성하거나 파괴할 수 없습니다.

camera-model.md/disconnection/0.text: `Camera::Private::disconnect()`는 현재 상태가 `CameraRunning`일 때만 `CameraConfigured`를 저장하며, 다른 상태에서는 이 저장을 생략합니다. 이후 상태와 관계없이 `disconnected_`를 `true`로 설정합니다. 주석에 따르면 상태 변경의 목적은 하드웨어가 제거될 때 카메라가 실행 중이었다면 애플리케이션이 카메라를 삭제하기 전에 자원을 해제하고 `release()`를 호출할 수 있도록 하는 것입니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/0.text: `CameraManager`는 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며, 애플리케이션에 카메라 접근을 제공하고 카메라 객체를 소유하면서 핫플러그와 핫언플러그에 따른 수명을 관리하는 libcamera의 진입점입니다. `CameraManager` 인스턴스는 한 번에 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 추가 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

camera-model.md/responsibility/1.text: `Camera`는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 모델링하며, 장치의 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스입니다. libcamera는 `std::shared_ptr`로 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 `create()`로 생성해야 합니다. `Camera`의 생성자와 소멸자는 수동 생성과 파괴를 막기 위해 비공개입니다.

camera-model.md/shutdown/2.text: 애플리케이션은 `createRequest()`로 요청을 할당한 뒤 큐에 넣기 전에 캡처 버퍼를 적어도 하나 채워야 합니다. `Camera::queueRequest()`는 카메라 상태·소유 카메라·요청 상태·제어 정보 검사 뒤에 버퍼 존재와 활성 스트림을 검사하며, 버퍼가 없거나 버퍼의 스트림이 활성 상태가 아니면 `-EINVAL`을 반환합니다. 큐에 넣은 요청의 완료는 `requestCompleted` 신호로 알립니다.

request-lifecycle.md/callback-depth/6.text: 변경 검증 계획에서는 발신자와 요청 소유자가 완료 및 해제 시점을 협의하고, 별도의 `ConnectionTypeQueued` 수신자마다 마지막 사용을 추적하고 동기화합니다. 모든 지연 수신자의 마지막 사용을 확인하기 전에는 삭제나 재사용으로 전달 대상의 수명을 끊지 않습니다.

request-lifecycle.md/callback-order/0.text: `PipelineHandler::completeBuffer`는 `bufferCompleted.emit` 뒤에 `Request::Private::completeBuffer`를 호출해 `pending_`에서 버퍼를 제거하고 버퍼의 요청 연결을 해제하며, `ConnectionTypeDirect` 콜백은 송신자 스레드에서 즉시 동기 실행되므로 내부 갱신 전에 실행될 수 있습니다. 호출자는 `bufferCompleted` 신호만으로 요청 완료나 삭제·재사용 시점을 판단해서는 안 되며, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼를 유효하게 유지해야 합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/callback-order/2.text: B의 `Request::addBuffer`가 A 버퍼의 직접 `bufferCompleted` 수신자 안에서 같은 버퍼의 연결을 B로 바꾸면, 뒤따르는 A의 내부 `completeBuffer`가 `setRequest(nullptr)`로 B 연결을 지울 수 있습니다. 지연된 수신자가 포인터를 마지막으로 사용하는 시점은 별도 수명 항목과 대조합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/callback-order/3.text: `Request::Private::completeBuffer()`는 `pending_`에서 버퍼를 지운 뒤 `setRequest(nullptr)`을 호출하지만, `doCancelRequest()`는 대기 중인 각 버퍼를 취소하고 완료 신호를 보낸 뒤 `pending_.clear()`를 호출하며 같은 연결 해제는 호출하지 않습니다. `FrameBuffer::request()`가 반환하는 포인터는 `Request::addBuffer()`로 연결된 때부터 버퍼가 완료될 때까지만 유효하므로, 취소 뒤 저장된 값이 비널이어도 유효한 `Request` 포인터나 소유권 또는 수명 연장으로 해석해서는 안 됩니다.

request-lifecycle.md/callback-order/4.text: 호출자는 `Request::addBuffer()`에 전달한 버퍼가 요청 완료 콜백까지 유효하도록 해야 하며, `Object::invokeMethod()`에 포인터 인수를 전달할 때는 호출된 메서드가 실행될 때까지 그 포인터가 유효하도록 해야 합니다. 유효한 fence가 신호되지 않아 요청이 타임아웃되면 애플리케이션은 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 `FrameBuffer::releaseFence()`로 fence를 회수해야 합니다. 조사 계획으로는 기존 실행에서 정상 완료와 일괄 취소 각각의 신호와 `pending_` 처리 순서, 버퍼의 fence 상태, 재사용 시 `Request::addBuffer()`의 반환값과 그에 따른 분기를 관찰합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/1.text: `Camera::createRequest()` 호출자는 반환된 `Request`의 소유권을 받으며 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 `Request::reuse()`로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/4.text: 마지막 버퍼 알림은 관찰했지만 요청 완료 콜백은 아직 관찰하지 못한 경우, 그 관측만으로 내부 추적 갱신이나 `completeRequest` 호출이 아직 남았다고 단정할 수 없습니다. 이 알림은 버퍼 유효성 유지 기한이 끝났다는 근거가 아니므로, 버퍼 유효성을 깨뜨리는 해제나 다른 요청에 연결하는 작업의 안전성을 알림만으로 판정할 수 없습니다. 모든 재사용이 일괄적으로 금지되는 것은 아니며, 다른 요청에 연결할 수 있는지는 적용되는 API와 동기화 계약 및 버퍼 유효성 유지를 별도로 대조해야 합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/9.text: 앞의 정상 완료 예와 별도로, 제출 큐의 선두 요청 A와 요청 B가 모두 `RequestPending`인 시점에 파이프라인 핸들러가 `completeRequest(B)` 대신 `cancelRequest(B)`를 호출하는 경우입니다. `Request::Private::doCancelRequest`는 B의 `pending_` 버퍼를 각각 취소하고 `bufferCompleted`를 발생시킨 뒤 `cancelled_`를 `true`로 설정하고 `pending_`를 비웁니다. `cancelRequest`는 `cancel` 다음에 `completeRequest`를 호출하며, `Request::Private::complete`는 B의 상태로 `RequestCancelled`를 선택합니다. 선두 A가 여전히 `RequestPending`이면 B의 애플리케이션 반환은 지연되며, 버퍼 수명과 핸들러의 요청 접근에는 앞에서 설명한 공통 규칙이 적용됩니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/10.text: `Request::addBuffer()`에 유효한 `Fence`를 전달하면 성공 시 소유권이 `buffer`로 이동하지만, 실패 시에는 전달한 `fence`가 수정되지 않고 소유권도 넘어가지 않습니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/11.text: 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 `FrameBuffer::releaseFence()`로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/resources/12.text: `Request::ReuseBuffers`는 `addBuffer()`로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 유지하여 재사용하지만, 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용하는 경우 이 플래그를 사용하지 않아야 한다는 권고가 있습니다(`should not be used`).

request-lifecycle.md/review/1.text: 기존 실행에서 `Request::reuse` 호출 전과 완료 후의 `status_`·`controls_`·`metadata_` 상태를 기록하고, `status_`에 RequestPending이 대입되는 코드 지점을 함께 기록하는 방안을 제안합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/review/9.text: 유효하게 dequeue된 버퍼의 `V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR`와 FrameError를 기록하고, UVC가 해당 상태를 유지한 채 completeBuffer 다음에 completeRequest를 호출하는 경로를 확인합니다. pending에서 버퍼가 한 번 제거되는 횟수와 요청의 제출·완료 통지 순서, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되는 수명을 기록하며, 다른 취소 원인이 없을 때 가능한 RequestComplete를 FrameError와 별도로 기록합니다.

request-lifecycle.md/review/11.text: 허용된 doQueueRequests 재진입에서는 pop과 투입 순서 및 request별 투입 횟수를 기록해 중복 투입이 없는지 확인하고, 같은 함수의 콜백 중첩 진입은 별도 허용 문서 없이 하지 않습니다. Direct와 지연된 Queued 수신의 현재·수신 스레드, cookie, sequence, 콜백 진입·복귀, stop 전후와 객체 수명을 기록하며, 실행 중 접근 검사를 통과한 `Camera::stop`이 `PipelineHandler::stop`을 ConnectionTypeBlocking으로 호출하는 정상 경로에 해당 실행이 도달했는지와 Blocking 반환 및 별도 Queued 수신자의 마지막 사용·종료를 구분해 확인하고, `Signal` 발신자가 포인터·참조의 유효성을 유지하며 요청 소유자가 삭제·재사용 전에 모든 지연 수신자의 마지막 사용을 완료·해제 협의로 동기화하는지 검증하고 요청 완료 신호나 한 핸들러의 복귀를 모든 지연 수신자의 사용 종료로 간주하지 않습니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/1.text: `Request::addBuffer`가 성공하면 유효한 `Fence`의 소유권은 `buffer`(`FrameBuffer`)로 이동합니다. 이때 `fence`는 `buffer`로 옮겨집니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/2.text: `addBuffer`가 실패하면 `fence`의 소유권은 가져가지 않으며, 전달받은 `fence`는 변경되지 않고 그대로 유지됩니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/3.text: 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패합니다. 이때 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남아 있으며, 애플리케이션은 다른 요청에 버퍼를 재사용하기 전에 `FrameBuffer::releaseFence()`로 이 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/4.text: `Request::reuse`는 `flags`에 `ReuseBuffers`가 설정된 경우 `bufferMap_`의 각 버퍼마다 `buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)`를 호출해 그 버퍼를 현재 요청에 연결한 뒤, `_d()->pending_`에 그 버퍼를 추가합니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/5.text: `Request::reuse()`에서 `flags & ReuseBuffers`가 거짓이면 else 분기가 실행되며, 이때 `bufferMap_.clear()`를 호출해 `bufferMap_`의 모든 항목을 비웁니다.

camera-requests.md/lifetime/7.text: `Request::ReuseBuffers` 플래그는 `Request::reuse()` 호출 시 `addBuffer()`로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 다시 사용하여 기존 버퍼를 유지합니다. 다만 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용되지 않으며, 소스 주석은 펜스를 사용하는 경우 이 플래그를 피하도록 권고합니다.

camera-requests.md/request/0.text: `createRequest`는 새로 만든 빈 `Request` 객체를 `std::unique_ptr<Request>`로 반환하며, 오류가 나면 `nullptr`을 반환합니다. 반환된 객체의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 이를 삭제할 책임을 가집니다. 요청은 완료 핸들러에서 삭제되거나, `Request::reuse()`로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용될 수 있습니다.

request-diagnosis.md/configuration-failu.text: `CameraConfiguration::validate()`의 `Adjusted`는 구성이 유효하도록 조정된 상태이며, 임의의 스트림에서 파라미터가 변경되거나 스트림 구성이 삭제될 수 있습니다.

catalog/2231a262175b6a27.text: CameraManager 인스턴스는 동시에 하나만 존재해야 합니다. 기존 인스턴스를 먼저 삭제하지 않고 두 번째 인스턴스를 생성하면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다. CameraManager::start()의 시작이 확인되면 애플리케이션은 카메라 관리자가 중지되거나 해당 카메라가 시스템에서 분리될 때까지 시스템의 카메라를 나열하고 사용할 수 있습니다. 호출자는 CameraManager::cameras()와 CameraManager::get()을 호출하기 전에 카메라 매니저가 실행 중인지 확인해야 합니다.

catalog/2231a262175b6a27/en.text: Only one CameraManager instance must exist at a time. Creating a second instance without first deleting the existing instance results in undefined behavior. Once the start of CameraManager::start() is confirmed, the application can list and use cameras in the system until the camera manager is stopped or the camera is disconnected from the system. The caller must ensure that the camera manager is running before calling CameraManager::cameras() and CameraManager::get().

catalog/4f1ec0014a118254.text: Camera는 하나의 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 모델링합니다. 장치 구성과 제어, 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주 인터페이스이며, libcamera가 공개하는 중심 객체입니다. libcamera는 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 std::shared_ptr<>로 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 create()로 생성해야 합니다. Camera의 생성자와 소멸자는 비공개이므로 인스턴스를 수동으로 생성하거나 파괴할 수 없습니다.

catalog/4f1ec0014a118254/en.text: Camera models a camera capable of producing one or more image streams from a single image source. It is the main interface for configuring and controlling the device and capturing image streams, and is the central object exposed by libcamera. libcamera manages the lifetime of camera instances with std::shared_ptr<>, and instances must be created with create(), which returns a shared pointer. The constructors and destructor of Camera are private, so instances cannot be created or destroyed manually.

catalog/3e36f02a0f5b1ba2.text: Camera::createRequest()가 반환한 요청의 소유권은 호출자에게 전달되며, 호출자가 요청을 삭제해야 합니다. 호출자는 새 요청을 만드는 대신 같은 요청을 다시 큐에 넣으려면 큐에 넣기 전에 Request::reuse()를 호출하여 요청 상태와 연결된 컨트롤을 초기화해야 합니다. Request::reuse(ReuseFlag)는 ReuseBuffers를 지정하면 addBuffer()로 추가한 기존 버퍼를 유지해 재사용하고, 지정하지 않으면 bufferMap_을 비웁니다.

catalog/3e36f02a0f5b1ba2/en.text: Ownership of the request returned by Camera::createRequest() is transferred to the caller, and the caller must delete the request. To requeue the same request instead of creating a new one, the caller must call Request::reuse() before queueing it to reset the request state and associated controls. Request::reuse(ReuseFlag) retains and reuses the existing buffers added with addBuffer() if ReuseBuffers is specified, and clears bufferMap_ otherwise.

catalog/d582b0220a378ad1.text: CameraManager는 장치를 열거하고 파이프라인 관리자와 연결하며, 애플리케이션에 카메라 접근을 제공하고 카메라 객체를 소유하면서 핫플러그와 핫언플러그에 따른 수명을 관리하는 libcamera의 진입점입니다. CameraManager 인스턴스는 한 번에 하나만 존재할 수 있으며, 기존 인스턴스를 삭제하기 전에 추가 인스턴스를 만들면 동작이 정의되지 않습니다.

catalog/d582b0220a378ad1/en.text: CameraManager is the entry point to libcamera, enumerating devices, associating them with pipeline managers, providing applications with access to cameras, owning camera objects, and managing their lifetimes in response to hot-plugging and hot-unplugging. Only one CameraManager instance may exist at a time, and creating an additional instance before deleting the existing instance results in undefined behavior.

catalog/6b62f2d56571bfff.text: Camera는 단일 이미지 소스에서 하나 이상의 이미지 스트림을 생성할 수 있는 카메라를 모델링하며, 장치의 설정과 제어 및 이미지 스트림 캡처를 위한 주요 인터페이스입니다. libcamera는 std::shared_ptr로 카메라 인스턴스의 수명을 관리하며, 인스턴스는 공유 포인터를 반환하는 create()로 생성해야 합니다. Camera의 생성자와 소멸자는 수동 생성과 파괴를 막기 위해 비공개입니다. Request는 애플리케이션이 프레임마다 버퍼와 컨트롤을 연결하고 카메라 장치의 처리를 위해 큐에 넣을 수 있게 하는 객체입니다.

catalog/6b62f2d56571bfff/en.text: Camera models a camera capable of producing one or more image streams from a single image source and is the main interface for configuring and controlling the device and capturing image streams. libcamera manages the lifetime of camera instances using std::shared_ptr, and instances must be created with create(), which returns a shared pointer. The constructors and destructor of Camera are private to prevent manual creation and destruction. Request is an object that allows an application to associate buffers and controls for each frame and queue them for processing by the camera device.

catalog/d1b6939731c3b5c0.text: 애플리케이션은 createRequest()로 요청을 할당한 뒤 큐에 넣기 전에 캡처 버퍼를 적어도 하나 채워야 합니다. Camera::queueRequest()는 카메라 상태·소유 카메라·요청 상태·제어 정보 검사 뒤에 버퍼 존재와 활성 스트림을 검사하며, 버퍼가 없거나 버퍼의 스트림이 활성 상태가 아니면 -EINVAL을 반환합니다. 큐에 넣은 요청의 완료는 requestCompleted 신호로 알립니다.

catalog/d1b6939731c3b5c0/en.text: After allocating a request with createRequest(), the application must fill it with at least one capture buffer before queuing it. After checking the camera state, the owning camera, the request state, and the control information, Camera::queueRequest() checks for the presence of buffers and active streams and returns -EINVAL if there are no buffers or a buffer's stream is not active. Completion of a queued request is signaled through the requestCompleted signal.

catalog/7b6ae714b7eca191.text: Camera::Private::disconnect()는 현재 상태가 CameraRunning일 때만 CameraConfigured를 저장하며, 다른 상태에서는 이 저장을 생략합니다. 이후 상태와 관계없이 disconnected_를 true로 설정합니다. 주석에 따르면 상태 변경의 목적은 하드웨어가 제거될 때 카메라가 실행 중이었다면 애플리케이션이 카메라를 삭제하기 전에 자원을 해제하고 release()를 호출할 수 있도록 하는 것입니다.

catalog/7b6ae714b7eca191/en.text: Camera::Private::disconnect() stores CameraConfigured only when the current state is CameraRunning, and skips this store in other states. Afterward, the function sets disconnected_ to true regardless of the state. According to the comment, the purpose of the state change is to allow the application to free resources and call release() before deleting the camera if the camera was running when the hardware was removed.

catalog/66a1e90cc2798e1a.text: Camera::createRequest() 호출자는 반환된 Request의 소유권을 받으며 삭제할 책임이 있습니다. 호출자는 완료 핸들러에서 요청을 삭제하거나 Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용할 수 있습니다. Request::addBuffer()는 버퍼 참조를 요청에 저장하며, 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 버퍼가 유효하도록 해야 합니다. 파이프라인 핸들러는 completeRequest() 또는 cancelRequest()가 반환된 뒤 해당 요청에 접근해서는 안 됩니다.

catalog/66a1e90cc2798e1a/en.text: The caller of Camera::createRequest() receives ownership of the returned Request and is responsible for deleting it. The caller may delete the request in the completion handler or reuse it after resetting its state with Request::reuse(). Request::addBuffer() stores a reference to the buffer in the request, and the caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is called. The pipeline handler must not access the request after completeRequest() or cancelRequest() returns.

catalog/428133d2002e0ebe.text: 마지막 버퍼 알림은 관찰했지만 요청 완료 콜백은 아직 관찰하지 못한 경우, 그 관측만으로 내부 추적 갱신이나 completeRequest 호출이 아직 남았다고 단정할 수 없습니다. 이 알림은 버퍼 유효성 유지 기한이 끝났다는 근거가 아니므로, 버퍼 유효성을 깨뜨리는 해제나 다른 요청에 연결하는 작업의 안전성을 알림만으로 판정할 수 없습니다. 모든 재사용이 일괄적으로 금지되는 것은 아니며, 다른 요청에 연결할 수 있는지는 적용되는 API와 동기화 계약 및 버퍼 유효성 유지를 별도로 대조해야 합니다.

catalog/428133d2002e0ebe/en.text: If the last buffer notification has been observed but the request completion callback has not yet been observed, that observation alone does not establish that the internal tracking update or the completeRequest call is still pending. This notification is not evidence that the period for which the buffer must remain valid has ended, so the notification alone cannot establish whether releasing it in a way that invalidates the buffer or attaching it to another request is safe. Reuse is not categorically prohibited; whether it can be attached to another request must be checked separately against the applicable API and synchronization contracts and the requirement to maintain buffer validity.

catalog/9ca84b17981ea70b.text: 앞의 정상 완료 예와 별도로, 제출 큐의 선두 요청 A와 요청 B가 모두 RequestPending인 시점에 파이프라인 핸들러가 completeRequest(B) 대신 cancelRequest(B)를 호출하는 경우입니다. Request::Private::doCancelRequest는 B의 pending_ 버퍼를 각각 취소하고 bufferCompleted를 발생시킨 뒤 cancelled_를 true로 설정하고 pending_를 비웁니다. cancelRequest는 cancel 다음에 completeRequest를 호출하며, Request::Private::complete는 B의 상태로 RequestCancelled를 선택합니다. 선두 A가 여전히 RequestPending이면 B의 애플리케이션 반환은 지연되며, 버퍼 수명과 핸들러의 요청 접근에는 앞에서 설명한 공통 규칙이 적용됩니다.

catalog/9ca84b17981ea70b/en.text: Separate from the preceding normal completion example, this is a case where the pipeline handler calls cancelRequest(B) instead of completeRequest(B) when both request A at the front of the submission queue and request B are RequestPending. Request::Private::doCancelRequest cancels each of B's pending_ buffers and emits bufferCompleted, then sets cancelled_ to true and clears pending_. cancelRequest calls completeRequest after cancel, and Request::Private::complete selects RequestCancelled as B's status. If A at the front is still RequestPending, B's return to the application is delayed, and the common rules described earlier apply to buffer lifetime and the handler's access to the request.

catalog/22c7c2b6a74a048a.text: Request::addBuffer()에 유효한 Fence를 전달하면 성공 시 소유권이 buffer로 이동하지만, 실패 시에는 전달한 fence가 수정되지 않고 소유권도 넘어가지 않습니다. 버퍼에 연결된 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패하며, 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남습니다. 애플리케이션은 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 펜스를 회수해야 합니다.

catalog/22c7c2b6a74a048a/en.text: When a valid Fence is passed to Request::addBuffer(), ownership moves to buffer on success, but on failure the supplied fence is not modified and ownership is not transferred. If the fence associated with the buffer is not signalled, the request fails after a timeout, and the fence remains in the buffer. The application must retrieve the fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request.

catalog/0bc2ed875598ae28.text: Request::ReuseBuffers는 addBuffer()로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 유지하여 재사용하지만, 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용하지 않습니다. 펜스를 사용하는 경우 이 플래그를 사용하지 않아야 한다는 권고가 있습니다(should not be used).

catalog/0bc2ed875598ae28/en.text: Request::ReuseBuffers retains and reuses buffers previously added with addBuffer(), but does not reuse the fences associated with the buffers. There is a recommendation that this flag should not be used if fences are used (should not be used).

catalog/d6efc3e15c1549ac.text: PipelineHandler::completeBuffer는 bufferCompleted.emit 뒤에 Request::Private::completeBuffer를 호출해 pending_에서 버퍼를 제거하고 버퍼의 요청 연결을 해제하며, ConnectionTypeDirect 콜백은 송신자 스레드에서 즉시 동기 실행되므로 내부 갱신 전에 실행될 수 있습니다. 호출자는 bufferCompleted 신호만으로 요청 완료나 삭제·재사용 시점을 판단해서는 안 되며, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼를 유효하게 유지해야 합니다.

catalog/d6efc3e15c1549ac/en.text: PipelineHandler::completeBuffer calls Request::Private::completeBuffer after bufferCompleted.emit to remove the buffer from pending_ and dissociate it from the request. The ConnectionTypeDirect callback executes immediately and synchronously in the sender's thread, so it may run before the internal update. The caller must not rely on the bufferCompleted signal alone to determine whether the request is complete or when it can be deleted or reused, and must keep the buffer valid until the request completion callback.

catalog/eda43d64b0e0b4ec.text: B의 Request::addBuffer가 A 버퍼의 직접 bufferCompleted 수신자 안에서 같은 버퍼의 연결을 B로 바꾸면, 뒤따르는 A의 내부 completeBuffer가 setRequest(nullptr)로 B 연결을 지울 수 있습니다. 지연된 수신자가 포인터를 마지막으로 사용하는 시점은 별도 수명 항목과 대조합니다.

catalog/eda43d64b0e0b4ec/en.text: If B's Request::addBuffer changes the same buffer's association to B inside a direct bufferCompleted receiver for A's buffer, A's subsequent internal completeBuffer may clear the association with B using setRequest(nullptr). The time at which a deferred receiver last uses the pointer is checked against the separate lifetime item.

catalog/8fe40ecdeaf90dbe.text: Request::Private::completeBuffer()는 pending_에서 버퍼를 지운 뒤 setRequest(nullptr)을 호출하지만, doCancelRequest()는 대기 중인 각 버퍼를 취소하고 완료 신호를 보낸 뒤 pending_.clear()를 호출하며 같은 연결 해제는 호출하지 않습니다. FrameBuffer::request()가 반환하는 포인터는 Request::addBuffer()로 연결된 때부터 버퍼가 완료될 때까지만 유효하므로, 취소 뒤 저장된 값이 비널이어도 유효한 Request 포인터나 소유권 또는 수명 연장으로 해석해서는 안 됩니다.

catalog/8fe40ecdeaf90dbe/en.text: Request::Private::completeBuffer() removes the buffer from pending_ and then calls setRequest(nullptr), whereas doCancelRequest() cancels each pending buffer, emits a completion signal, and then calls pending_.clear() without making the same disconnection. The pointer returned by FrameBuffer::request() is valid only from the time the buffer is associated through Request::addBuffer() until the buffer completes, so even if the stored value is non-null after cancellation, it must not be interpreted as a valid Request pointer, ownership, or an extension of lifetime.

catalog/b9c8f331471bc4cd.text: 호출자는 Request::addBuffer()에 전달한 버퍼가 요청 완료 콜백까지 유효하도록 해야 하며, Object::invokeMethod()에 포인터 인수를 전달할 때는 호출된 메서드가 실행될 때까지 그 포인터가 유효하도록 해야 합니다. 유효한 fence가 신호되지 않아 요청이 타임아웃되면 애플리케이션은 버퍼를 다른 요청에서 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 fence를 회수해야 합니다. 조사 계획으로는 기존 실행에서 정상 완료와 일괄 취소 각각의 신호와 pending_ 처리 순서, 버퍼의 fence 상태, 재사용 시 Request::addBuffer()의 반환값과 그에 따른 분기를 관찰합니다.

catalog/b9c8f331471bc4cd/en.text: The caller must ensure that the buffer passed to Request::addBuffer() remains valid until the request completion callback, and, when passing a pointer argument to Object::invokeMethod(), must ensure that the pointer remains valid until the invoked method executes. If a request times out because a valid fence is not signalled, the application must retrieve the fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request. The investigation plan is to observe, in an existing run, the order of signals and pending_ processing for both normal completion and bulk cancellation, the buffer's fence state, and the return value of Request::addBuffer() upon reuse and the resulting branch.

catalog/333ccb32d947bf57.text: 변경 검증 계획에서는 발신자와 요청 소유자가 완료 및 해제 시점을 협의하고, 별도의 ConnectionTypeQueued 수신자마다 마지막 사용을 추적하고 동기화합니다. 모든 지연 수신자의 마지막 사용을 확인하기 전에는 삭제나 재사용으로 전달 대상의 수명을 끊지 않습니다. 소스 기반 조사 계획으로, Signal::emit()에서 수신자의 Object 유무, 연결 종류, 현재 스레드와 수신 스레드, 이벤트 루프, 요청과 버퍼의 상태를 기록하고 콜백 진입·복귀 및 카메라 정지 전후를 애플리케이션 표식으로 구분합니다. ConnectionTypeDirect의 재진입과 ConnectionTypeQueued의 지연을 조사하면서 전달된 포인터·참조의 유효성, Request::Private::completeBuffer()의 pending_.erase(buffer) 반환값과 다음 분기, 중복 완료 및 정지 후 요청 제출 여부를 확인합니다.

catalog/333ccb32d947bf57/en.text: In the change verification plan, the sender and request owner coordinate completion and release timing and track and synchronize the last use by each separate ConnectionTypeQueued receiver. They do not end the lifetime of the object passed by deleting or reusing it before confirming the last use by every delayed receiver. The source-based investigation plan is to record, at Signal::emit(), whether the receiver has an Object, the connection type, the current and receiver threads, the event loop, and the states of the request and buffer, and to distinguish callback entry and return and the periods before and after camera stop with application markers. While investigating ConnectionTypeDirect reentrancy and ConnectionTypeQueued delays, the plan is to check the validity of passed pointers and references, the return value of pending_.erase(buffer) in Request::Private::completeBuffer() and the subsequent branch, and whether duplicate completion or request submission after stop occurs.

catalog/29813f852f03a638.text: 조사 시 기존 Camera::queueRequest() 호출의 반환값을 기록 항목으로 제안합니다. 기존 실행에서 Request::reuse 호출 전과 완료 후의 status_·controls_·metadata_ 상태를 기록하고, status_에 RequestPending이 대입되는 코드 지점을 함께 기록하는 방안을 제안합니다. 기존 실행에서 선두 요청의 상태 조회식 req->status() 값을 조사 기록 항목으로 남길 것을 제안합니다.

catalog/29813f852f03a638/en.text: For the investigation, I propose recording the return value of the existing Camera::queueRequest() call. I propose recording the states of status_, controls_, and metadata_ before the existing Request::reuse call and after it completes, along with the code location where RequestPending is assigned to status_. I propose recording the value of the head request's status query expression req->status() during the existing execution as an investigation item.

catalog/1c4ddf4b516f4b9b.text: 유효하게 dequeue된 버퍼의 V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR와 FrameError를 기록하고, UVC가 해당 상태를 유지한 채 completeBuffer 다음에 completeRequest를 호출하는 경로를 확인합니다. pending에서 버퍼가 한 번 제거되는 횟수와 요청의 제출·완료 통지 순서, 요청 완료 콜백까지 버퍼가 유효하게 유지되는 수명을 기록하며, 다른 취소 원인이 없을 때 가능한 RequestComplete를 FrameError와 별도로 기록합니다.

catalog/1c4ddf4b516f4b9b/en.text: The plan is to record V4L2_BUF_FLAG_ERROR and FrameError for a validly dequeued buffer and check the path where UVC calls completeBuffer followed by completeRequest while retaining that status. The plan also records the count of buffer removals from pending, which should occur once, the order of request submission and completion notifications, and the period for which the buffer remains valid through the request completion callback. Any possible RequestComplete when there is no other cause of cancellation is recorded separately from FrameError.

catalog/5cdd59f9b84a5a89.text: createRequest는 새로 만든 빈 Request 객체를 std::unique_ptr<Request>로 반환하며, 오류가 나면 nullptr을 반환합니다. 반환된 객체의 소유권은 호출자에게 넘어가며, 호출자가 이를 삭제할 책임을 가집니다. 요청은 완료 핸들러에서 삭제되거나, Request::reuse()로 상태를 초기화한 뒤 재사용될 수 있습니다. 호출자는 Request::addBuffer로 한 요청에 같은 스트림의 버퍼를 둘 이상 연결해서는 안 되며, 한 요청은 스트림당 버퍼를 하나만 포함할 수 있습니다.

catalog/5cdd59f9b84a5a89/en.text: createRequest returns a newly created empty Request object as std::unique_ptr<Request>, and returns nullptr if an error occurs. Ownership of the returned object passes to the caller, who is responsible for deleting it. The request may be deleted in the completion handler, or reused after its state is reset with Request::reuse(). The caller must not add two or more buffers for the same stream to one request via Request::addBuffer, and a request can contain only one buffer per stream.

catalog/cd6e66c2ce8b9b8e.text: Request::addBuffer는 버퍼에 대한 참조를 요청에 저장합니다. 호출자는 요청 완료 콜백이 호출될 때까지 해당 버퍼가 유효하게 남아 있도록 보장해야 합니다. Request::addBuffer가 성공하면 유효한 Fence의 소유권은 buffer(FrameBuffer)로 이동합니다. 이때 fence는 buffer로 옮겨집니다.

catalog/cd6e66c2ce8b9b8e/en.text: Request::addBuffer stores a reference to the buffer in the request. The caller must ensure that the buffer remains valid until the request completion callback is invoked. If Request::addBuffer succeeds, ownership of the valid Fence moves to buffer (FrameBuffer). At that point, fence is moved to buffer.

catalog/bef82e569e5b5ab3.text: addBuffer가 실패하면 fence의 소유권은 가져가지 않으며, 전달받은 fence는 변경되지 않고 그대로 유지됩니다. 펜스가 신호되지 않으면 요청은 타임아웃 후 실패합니다. 이때 버퍼에는 펜스가 그대로 남아 있으며, 애플리케이션은 다른 요청에 버퍼를 재사용하기 전에 FrameBuffer::releaseFence()로 이 펜스를 회수해야 합니다. Request::reuse는 flags에 ReuseBuffers가 설정된 경우 bufferMap_의 각 버퍼마다 buffer->_d()->setRequest(this)를 호출해 그 버퍼를 현재 요청에 연결한 뒤, _d()->pending_에 그 버퍼를 추가합니다.

catalog/bef82e569e5b5ab3/en.text: If addBuffer fails, ownership of fence is not taken, and the received fence remains unchanged. If the fence is not signalled, the request fails after a timeout. In this case, the fence remains in the buffer, and the application must retrieve this fence with FrameBuffer::releaseFence() before reusing the buffer in another request. Request::reuse calls buffer->_d()->setRequest(this) for each buffer in bufferMap_ when ReuseBuffers is set in flags, to associate that buffer with the current request, and then adds that buffer to _d()->pending_.

catalog/ee2812d177feff9b.text: Request::reuse()에서 flags & ReuseBuffers가 거짓이면 else 분기가 실행되며, 이때 bufferMap_.clear()를 호출해 bufferMap_의 모든 항목을 비웁니다. Request::reuse는 status_를 RequestPending으로 설정한 뒤, controls_와 _d()->metadata_를 각각 clear()합니다. Request::ReuseBuffers 플래그는 Request::reuse() 호출 시 addBuffer()로 이전에 추가한 버퍼를 다시 사용하여 기존 버퍼를 유지합니다. 다만 버퍼에 연결된 펜스는 재사용되지 않으며, 소스 주석은 펜스를 사용하는 경우 이 플래그를 피하도록 권고합니다.

catalog/ee2812d177feff9b/en.text: In Request::reuse(), the else branch runs when flags & ReuseBuffers is false, and bufferMap_.clear() is called to clear all entries of bufferMap_. Request::reuse sets status_ to RequestPending, then calls clear() on each of controls_ and _d()->metadata_. When Request::reuse() is called, the Request::ReuseBuffers flag reuses the buffers previously added with addBuffer() and keeps the existing buffers. However, fences attached to buffers are not reused, and the source comment recommends avoiding this flag when fences are used.

catalog/3588f1bd7883e248.text: CameraConfiguration::validate()의 Adjusted는 구성이 유효하도록 조정된 상태이며, 임의의 스트림에서 파라미터가 변경되거나 스트림 구성이 삭제될 수 있습니다. Adjusted를 받은 호출자는 구성을 주의 깊게 확인해야 합니다.

catalog/3588f1bd7883e248/en.text: Adjusted from CameraConfiguration::validate() means the configuration has been adjusted so that it is valid; parameters may have changed for any stream, or stream configurations may have been removed. A caller that receives Adjusted must check the configuration carefully.

\class Signal
 * \brief Generic signal and slot communication mechanism
 *
 * Signals and slots are a language construct aimed at communication between
 * objects through the observer pattern without the need for boilerplate code.
 * See http://doc.qt.io/qt-6/signalsandslots.html for more information.
 *
 * Signals model events that can be observed from objects unrelated to the event
 * source. Slots are functions that are called in response to a signal. Signals
 * can be connected to and disconnected from slots dynamically at runtime. When
 * a signal is emitted, all connected slots are called sequentially in the order
 * they have been connected.
 *
 * Signals are defined with zero, one or more typed parameters. They are emitted
 * with a value for each of the parameters, and those values are passed to the
 * connected slots.
 *
 * Slots are normal static or class member functions. In order to be connected
 * to a signal, their signature must match the signal type (taking the same
 * arguments as the signal and returning void).
 *
 * Connecting a signal to a slot results in the slot being called with the
 * arguments passed to the emit() function when the signal is emitted. Multiple
 * slots can be connected to the same signal, and multiple signals can connected
 * to the same slot.
 *
 * When a slot belongs to an instance of the Object class, the slot is called
 * in the context of the thread that the object is bound to. If the signal is
 * emitted from the same thread, the slot will be called synchronously, before
 * Signal::emit() returns. If the signal is emitted from a different thread,
 * the slot will be called asynchronously from the object's thread's event
 * loop, after the Signal::emit() function returns, with a copy of the signal's
 * arguments. The emitter shall thus ensure that any pointer or reference
 * passed through the signal will remain valid after the signal is emitted.
 *
 * Duplicate connections between a signal and a slot are not expected and use of
 * the Object class to manage signals will enforce this restriction.
 */

// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC-BY-SA-4.0

/**
 * \page thread-safety Reentrancy and Thread-Safety
 *
 * Through the documentation, several terms are used to define how classes and
 * their member functions can be used from multiple threads.
 *
 * - A **reentrant** function may be called simultaneously from multiple
 *   threads if and only if each invocation uses a different instance of the
 *   class. This is the default for all member functions not explictly marked
 *   otherwise.
 *
 * - \anchor thread-safe A **thread-safe** function may be called
 *   simultaneously from multiple threads on the same instance of a class. A
 *   thread-safe function is thus reentrant. Thread-safe functions may also be
 *   called simultaneously with any other reentrant function of the same class
 *   on the same instance.
 *
 * \internal
 * - \anchor thread-bound A **thread-bound** function may be called only from
 *   the thread that the class instances lives in (see section \ref
 *   thread-objects). For instances of classes that do not derive from the
 *   Object class, this is the thread in which the instance was created. A
 *   thread-bound function is not thread-safe, and may or may not be reentrant.
 * \endinternal
 *
 * Neither reentrancy nor thread-safety, in this context, mean that a function
 * may be called simultaneously from the same thread, for instance from a
 * callback invoked by the function. This may deadlock and isn't allowed unless
 * separately documented.
 *
 * \if internal
 * A class is defined as reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound if all its
 * member functions are reentrant, thread-safe or thread-bound respectively.
 * \else
 * A class is defined as reentrant or thread-safe if all its member functions
 * are reentrant or thread-safe respectively.
 * \endif
 * Some member functions may additionally be documented as having additional
 * thread-related attributes.
 *
 * Most classes are reentrant but not thread-safe, as making them fully
 * thread-safe would incur locking costs considered prohibitive for the
 * expected use cases.
 */

sources.source_quote:
\fn PipelineHandler::match(DeviceEnumerator *enumerator)
 * \brief Match media devices and create camera instances
 * \param[in] enumerator The enumerator providing all media devices found in the
 * system
 *
 * This function is the main entry point of the pipeline handler. It is called
 * by the camera manager with the \a enumerator passed as an argument. It shall
 * acquire from the \a enumerator all the media devices it needs for a single
 * pipeline, create one or multiple Camera instances and register them with the
 * camera manager.
 *
 * If all media devices needed by the pipeline handler are found, they must all
 * be acquired by a call to MediaDevice::acquire(). This function shall then
 * create the corresponding Camera instances, store them internally, and return
 * true. Otherwise it shall not acquire any media device (or shall release all
 * the media devices is has acquired by calling MediaDevice::release()) and
 * return false.
 *
 * If multiple instances of a pipeline are available in the system, the
 * PipelineHandler class will be instantiated once per instance, and its match()
 * function called for every instance. Each call shall acquire media devices for
 * one pipeline instance, until all compatible media devices are exhausted.
 *
 * If this function returns true, a new instance of the pipeline handler will
 * be created and its match() function called.
 *
 * \context This function is called from the CameraManager thread.
 *
 * \return true if media devices have been acquired and camera instances
 * created, or false otherwise
 */

findings.claim_quote: `PipelineHandler::match()`는 `CameraManager` 스레드에서 호출되며, `true`를 반환하면 새로운 `PipelineHandler` 인스턴스가 생성되고 그 인스턴스의 `match()`가 호출됩니다.

 *

 * the \a buffer part of the \a request. It notifies applications of buffer
 * completion and updates the request's internal buffer tracking. The request
 * is not completed automatically when the last buffer completes to give
 * pipeline handlers a chance to perform any operation that may still be
 * needed. They shall complete requests explicitly with completeRequest().
